protocol.py: 6 biology problems (4 errors, 1 warning, 1 note).

1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well B1 in slot 1: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 51:  p20.aspirate(2, source_plate["B1"])
   At line 51 the p20_single_gen2 draws 2 ul from buffer (well B1 in slot 1) with its tip 1
   mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 27 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well
   Plate 200 µL Flat reaches only 0.85 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air
   (this line did it 8 times, after 4 times in the liquid; 16 ul of air in all). The
   simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. These are mixing strokes: the
   tip stirs air, and the well is not mixed.
   Affected: well B1 in slot 1.
   Fix: Mix lower, with `well.bottom(0.5)`, so the tip is in the liquid. This well needs
   about 35 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [04200f34c5dc]

   Affected: well B2 in slot 1.
   Fix: Mix lower, with `well.bottom(0.5)`, so the tip is in the liquid. This well needs

3. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: water (well B3 in slot 1)
   line 57:  p20.aspirate(12, source_plate["B3"])
   At line 57 the tip went into water (well B3 in slot 1) while it still carried plasmid 1
   (well A1 in slot 1), plasmid 2 (well A2 in slot 1), plasmid 3 (well A3 in slot 1),
   plasmid 4 (well A4 in slot 1) and 9 more from an earlier step (this line did it 11
   times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from
   it then took the unwanted material along into 10 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6,
   A7, A8, A9 and 2 more in slot 2.
   Affected: well B3 in slot 1.
   Also reached 10 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 2 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 57 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing

   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.

5. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 7 stocks
   line 55:  p20.aspirate(5, source_plate[f"A{i}"])
   At line 55 the tip went into plasmid 1 (well A1 in slot 1), plasmid 2 (well A2 in slot
   1), plasmid 3 (well A3 in slot 1), plasmid 4 (well A4 in slot 1) and 3 more while it
   still carried buffer (well B1 in slot 1) and enzyme (well B2 in slot 1) from an earlier
   step (this line did it 7 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it
   in the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong
   there. Liquid drawn from them then took the unwanted material along into 7 other wells:
   wells A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10 and A11 in slot 2.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 1.
   Also reached 7 other wells: wells A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10 and A11 in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 55 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [4e921644a97d]

findings.title: The pipette draws air from well B1 in slot 1: the liquid is below the tip
findings.explanation: At line 51 the p20_single_gen2 draws 2 ul from buffer (well B1 in slot 1) with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 27 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat reaches only 0.85 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 8 times, after 4 times in the liquid; 16 ul of air in all).
